# MyChrome

> Keep browsing. Bring in AI when you need a hand. MyChrome lets an assistant work in the user's existing Google Chrome, hand a step back when it needs the user, and continue the same task after the user explicitly says to resume. It is a local MCP server and native macOS app with real mouse and keyboard input, adjustable pace and optional personal habit sampling.

## Product and setup

- [Product website](https://shuaige121.github.io/mychrome-mcp/): same-page assistance, user handoff and personal input pace.

## Working together on the same page

- The user keeps browsing normally and calls in the assistant when help is needed. Use the page title or URL supplied in the existing conversation; read the actual page and identify the target and relevant website account before acting.
- Carry out the authorized steps and verify the visible result. Ask when the target is ambiguous, information is missing or a new decision is required; do not ask again at every click.
- For a password, verification code or challenge the user can handle, hand the page back. Wait for an explicit instruction to continue, then reread the page and resume the original task.
- Task examples include organizing the user's LinkedIn page, checking their Facebook notifications or messages, and distributing their finished article to the Facebook, 小红书, Reddit and LinkedIn accounts they specify. These are suggested requests, not verified platform case studies.

## Personal input pace

- Choose task-selected input, key-by-key typing or paste. Set the pace of typing, mouse movement and scrolling from 0.5× to 3×. Explicit user settings apply to subsequent actions.
- Optional experimental habit sampling records three minutes of keyboard and mouse rhythm and fits timing statistics for subsequent typing and movement. Users can enable or disable its use, resample or delete it. Insufficient samples retain default parameters.
- Habit sampling stores rhythm statistics rather than typed text or a screen video. It does not clone the user's complete behavior or guarantee that websites will accept automation.

## Setup, controls and data

- Apple Silicon, macOS 13+, Google Chrome in /Applications, supported Node.js and Xcode Command Line Tools. Node 24+ is recommended; 20.19+ and 22.13+ are also supported.
- Install with `bash scripts/setup.sh` from a source checkout. This release is not published to npm.
- Codex and Claude Code support browser tools. Conversations created through the native app support live assistant text and direct replies for both clients. Existing external Codex conversations need a supported integration and associated thread; existing external Claude Code conversations cannot be associated and must continue in their original client.
- Use **新对话 (New conversation)** to select an installed, logged-in Codex or Claude Code CLI, an available model, supported reasoning effort and a working directory. The model choices come from that CLI. An initial task is optional; the new conversation is separate from existing client conversations.
- Physical input is serialized. During takeover, ordinary user input is intercepted; double Esc cancels the active agent. Global pause prevents subsequent input. Stop does not undo actions already sent.
- Website routine recording is on by default. Local metadata may reveal usage context; typed and selected values are not saved as replay defaults. Runs need fresh parameters and an explicit tab, stop on mismatches, and do not prove the broader task succeeded.
- Page content returned through MCP goes to the AI client and is handled under its settings. Local operation is not a promise that all task data remains on-device.
- Website compatibility depends on the actual workflow. On a 403, denied access or rate limit, stop and report the restriction; do not retry or switch tools to bypass it. User handoff is not a promise that blocked access can be restored.
